claim: PUMS's Fall 2027 application calendar gives the start of classes as 13 September 2026 — a 2026 day printed on a 2027 calendar — and puts orientation week at 6–12 September 2027.
excerpt: Start of classes: 13 Sep 2026 […] Orientation week for incoming students in Poznan: 6 - 12 Sep 2027
interpretation: The date is internally impossible: a 2027 intake cannot begin classes in September 2026. What makes this page the more informative of the two is its orientation week, 6–12 September 2027, because PUMS runs classes after orientation rather than during it — for 2026/27 it published orientation 7–13 September and classes 14 September. That pattern points at Monday 13 September 2027, which would make the '13 Sep' here the right day with the wrong year. It is still an inference, the string appears on no PUMS page, and the product records no date.

notes: Neither PUMS page carries a last-updated stamp, so there is no way to tell which of the two figures is the stale one.

claim: PUMS's medicine admission-requirements page, under a heading for Fall 2027 entry, gives the start of classes as 6 September 2027.
interpretation: This has the right year, which makes it the tempting one, and it collides with the university's own orientation week of 6–12 September 2027 on the calendar page recorded as ev-pums-calendar-class-start. Classes cannot start on the Monday orientation begins. So the page with the correct year is not thereby the correct page, and neither figure can be published as printed. This is the specific reason the entry carries no date rather than the later or the more plausible one: a medical degree is a six-year commitment and a student moving to Poznan a week early or a week late is a real cost.

notes: The resolution is not ours to make; it needs the PUMS admissions office. The country record says so and records what the evidence points at without publishing it.

publisher: NAWA (Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange)
claim: An IB certificate needs no individual recognition statement from NAWA: it is automatically recognised for the purpose of applying to first-cycle and long-cycle studies in Poland.
excerpt: The NAWA’s Director individual recognition statement is not required in the case of secondary school certificates issued in EU, OECD or EFTA member countries, those included in international agreements on recognition of education (e.g. agreements with China or Ukraine) as well as IB and EB certificates. Those documents are automatically recognised for the purpose of applying for admission to first-cycle studies or long-cycle studies
interpretation: This closes the question the country profile left open: NAWA's position on the IB for admission, as distinct from recognition of secondary education. Automatic recognition is not admission; each university still applies its own conversion and subject rules.

claim: Admissions in Poland are run by each higher education institution, and candidates apply directly to the institution of their choice.
excerpt: Admissions to the study programs are administrated by the higher educations institutions (HEIs) and candidates apply directly to the institution of their choice.
interpretation: No national portal. Each university runs its own online registration (IRK) with its own dates, fee and requirements.

interpretation: Polish-taught only. English-taught programmes may charge EU citizens, and whether they do is programme by programme — see ev-uw-tuition-2026-27.

claim: The University of Warsaw's 2026/27 fee schedule for English-taught programmes prints separate prices for EU/EFTA and non-EU citizens, and some programmes are free of charge for EU/EFTA citizens while others charge them.
excerpt: Citizens of EU/EFTA (EEA parties) and Switzerland: free of charge […] Citizens of Non-EU/EFTA (EEA parties) and Switzerland: 5,500 EUR
interpretation: The point for a pamphlet is the pattern, not the table: at the same university an English-taught programme can be free for an EU citizen or cost several thousand euros. Check the programme's own line. Prices are for 2026/27; 2027/28 was not yet published.

notes: A three-page PDF whose table does not survive text extraction cleanly; the column pairing of individual prices was not relied on here, only that both free-of-charge and charged EU prices appear.
